0.0.n: This time word tells when the action happened.

0.1.n: Adds last year as another occasion when they did it.

0.2.n: Casual past form of やる; the activity is understood from context.

0.3.n: Casual form of もの, giving a reason or reminding someone of a shared fact.

0.4.n: Invites agreement about something both speakers remember.

1.0.n: Casual past form of やる, used here to confirm the previous speaker’s statement.

2.0.n: Introduces a contrast with what was just said.

2.1.n: Sets the time for the experience being described.

2.2.n: Marks last year as the topic, contrasting it with this year.

2.3.n: 仮装する becomes 仮装させる to express making or getting someone else to dress up.

2.4.n: Turns 仮装させる into an activity that can be described as easy; the following subject marker が is omitted.

2.5.n: Describes the activity as requiring little effort.

2.6.n: だっ is the form of だ used before た to make だった.

2.7.n: Completes だった, placing the description in the past.

2.8.n: Adds an explanatory tone; sentence-ending のよ can sound feminine.

2.9.n: Emphasizes information the speaker is sharing with the listener.

3.0.n: A casual response showing agreement or that the listener is following along.

4.0.n: Casual shortened form of やっぱり, suggesting something expected or a choice ultimately made.

4.1.n: Sets the time for the costume choice being discussed.

4.2.n: Marks this year as the topic, contrasting it with last year.

4.3.n: Refers to all the people in the relevant group.

4.4.n: The name of the fictional characters whose costumes everyone wore; Japanese does not mark the plural here.

4.5.n: Marks the resulting identity with なる; here, the change is through costumes.

4.6.n: Past form of なる, literally becoming something; here it refers to taking on a character’s appearance.

4.7.n: Shortened form of explanatory の, adding background before the contrast.

4.8.n: Combines with ん as んだ to present an explanation; なった already marks the event as past.

4.9.n: Introduces the contrasting problem described in the next line.

5.0.n: 着る in its て-form plus negative くれる expresses that he will not wear it for the speaker.

5.2.n: Repeating the same present-negative phrase emphasizes his refusal, even though the English translation uses past tense.

0.lit: Last year too, we did it, after all, right!
0.tip: もんね reminds the listener of a shared fact and invites agreement.

1.tip: Repeating the same past-tense verb is a natural way to confirm what someone just said.

2.lit: But as for last year, getting him to dress up was easy, you see.
2.tip: させる shifts the action from dressing up yourself to getting someone else to dress up.

3.tip: うん is casual; はい is the more polite response.

4.lit: After all, as for this year, everyone became Minions, you see, but…
4.tip: ミニオンになった literally says they became Minions, but here it means they dressed as them.

5.lit: He won’t wear it for me. He won’t wear it for me.
5.tip: てくれない frames his refusal as not doing something the speaker wants him to do.
